title: Decision Practice
subtitle: Stop & Decide prompts to build active clinical judgment
howToUse: These decision points interrupt passive reading and force active thinking. For each scenario, pause and write your response. Then compare with the model response. Focus on (1) the immediate risk, (2) the safest first nursing action, and (3) what data you must check next.

decisions.title: Urinary output monitoring
decisions.scenario: You review the patient’s fluid balance chart and notice that urine output has been significantly lower than expected over the past two hours. The patient looks tired and reports feeling thirsty.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)
decisions.modelWhy: Low output may indicate renal impairment.

decisions.title: Wound dressing change
decisions.scenario: You prepare to change a surgical dressing. The patient is lying comfortably but looks concerned and asks whether the wound is healing properly. The old dressing is still in place, and you have not yet inspected the wound.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Pain assessment
decisions.scenario: The patient tells you their pain is 7 out of 10 and looks uncomfortable. They shift position frequently and say the pain is affecting their ability to rest. No pain relief has yet been administered.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Positioning for safety
decisions.scenario: A confused patient repeatedly tries to climb out of bed without assistance. They appear disoriented and do not respond to verbal reminders. The bed rails are down, and the call bell is out of reach.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

decisions.title: Feeding assistance
decisions.scenario: You assist a patient during a meal. As they begin eating, they suddenly start coughing and clearing their throat repeatedly. The patient looks distressed and pauses eating but does not stop on their own.
prompts: Your first action
Your reason (what risk are you preventing?)
What you will check next (one key assessment)

prompts: Your first action
